claims.statement: resolve_github_token routes GitHub token resolution by run source: sources carrying a mapped GitHub login (slack, linear, dashboard, schedule) prefer the triggering user's per-user OAuth token from the dashboard store — even in bot-token-only mode — so PRs and comments are attributed to that user.

When no valid per-user GitHub token is available, resolve_github_token falls back to a GitHub App installation token only in bot-token-only mode; in interactive mode it instead raises GitHubUserAuthRequired to force (re-)authentication rather than silently acting as the bot.

is_bot_token_only_mode() is true when LANGSMITH_API_KEY_PROD is set but neither X_SERVICE_AUTH_JWT_SECRET nor USER_ID_API_KEY_MAP is configured, meaning per-user OAuth tokens cannot be resolved and the GitHub App installation token is used for git operations.

Resolved GitHub tokens are cached only in process memory keyed by (thread_id, principal), where the principal isolates one user's token from another (login:/email:) and a distinct bot principal isolates installation tokens; tokens are never persisted and caching an unbound user token with no principal is refused.

Cached GitHub token entries expire on the token's own expiry (with a 60-second skew) or a hard 24-hour TTL cap, whichever comes first, and invalidate_cached_github_token clears a thread's entries when a stale/revoked token is detected.

GitHub App installation tokens are minted by signing a short-lived RS256 JWT with the App private key and exchanging it for an installation access token, cached in-process by a scope key of installation id, repository ids/names, and permissions, and reused until within a 10-minute margin of expiry that exceeds the proxy refresh window.

The dashboard authenticates browsers via GitHub App OAuth and a HS256 session JWT stored in the osw_session cookie signed with DASHBOARD_JWT_SECRET, valid for 7 days; require_session rejects requests without a valid session cookie and /me returns the signed-in identity plus is_admin.

The OAuth login/callback flow binds a random state nonce to the browser: /auth/login stores the nonce's HMAC in a signed state JWT and the raw nonce in a cookie, and /auth/callback verifies them with a constant-time compare before exchanging the code, resolving the login, enforcing the org gate, and issuing the session.

Post-login redirects are constrained by sanitize_redirect_to, which permits only same-origin relative paths or origins on the dashboard allowlist (DASHBOARD_BASE_URL plus DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) and blocks known open-redirect paths, preventing a login link from being steered to an attacker origin.

enforce_org_login_gate treats a nonempty ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS allowlist as fail-closed: it allows only an active member of at least one listed org, checking membership with a GitHub App installation token and rejecting API/token/membership failures; when the allowlist is empty it intentionally fails open but logs once per process that any GitHub account may log in and all logged-in users can read surfaced threads.

Cookie-authenticated dashboard mutations are CSRF-protected by an origin allowlist (require_same_origin / require_same_origin_for_mutations): safe methods are exempt and a request whose only credential is an explicit bearer GitHub token without a session cookie is exempt because a browser cannot forge it.

Desktop login uses PKCE so no session is placed on a loopback URL: the browser receives a short-lived handoff JWT carrying identity and the app's S256 challenge, and redeem_desktop_handoff mints the session only when presented the matching verifier via constant-time compare; cloud-terminal access uses a 60-second ticket bound to a specific thread_id and audience.

Slack accounts are linked to GitHub identities through verified Slack OIDC, and verify_team refuses identities from a different workspace when SLACK_TEAM_ID is configured (cross-workspace / Slack Connect refusal).

Auth-failure notices posted into a shared Slack thread are token-free and link only to build_settings_url() rather than a per-user GitHub auth URL, so nobody else in the thread can complete auth and bind the wrong account.

verify_github_signature authenticates GitHub webhooks by recomputing sha256=HMAC(GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, body) and comparing to X-Hub-Signature-256 with constant-time compare, failing closed (returns False) when the secret is unset, and is enforced by the GitHub webhook route.

verify_slack_signature validates the v0:timestamp:body HMAC against the Slack signature and additionally rejects requests whose timestamp is older than 300 seconds to block replay, failing closed when the signing secret is unset.

verify_linear_signature authenticates Linear webhooks by comparing the raw-body HMAC-SHA256 against the Linear-Signature header with constant-time compare, failing closed when LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset.

The publicly reachable /webhooks/run-complete route is authenticated by verify_run_complete_token against a shared secret (RUN_COMPLETE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) using constant-time compare, and is fail-closed: when the secret is unset every call is rejected and run-failure replies are disabled.

Persisted credentials are encrypted at rest with a MultiFernet built from TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which may be a most-recent-first key list so the first key encrypts and every key is tried for decryption to enable rotation; decrypt_token degrades to an empty string on an invalid token or missing key rather than raising.

The dashboard credential stores encrypt tokens before persistence via encrypt_token/decrypt_token, including GitHub OAuth access and refresh tokens in profiles.py and per-user, team, and Notion credentials.

When GitHub reports an unrecoverable refresh error (bad_refresh_token or unauthorized_client), the stored GitHub OAuth authorization is dropped so callers prompt a clean re-login instead of serving a known-stale access token.

Admin identity is derived from CONFIGURED_ADMINS (matched case-insensitively on email or login), and require_admin re-checks the triggering user against it at tool-call time so a thread whose metadata claims admin status cannot act on behalf of a non-admin.

is_observability_authorized grants team observability access to configured admins plus emails in OBSERVABILITY_AUTHORIZED_EMAILS, and the per-run gate _observability_authorized (kept uncached) decides whether team Datadog/LangSmith tools are exposed, so prompt-injected runs from untrusted contributors cannot reach the team's observability data.

Optional server-side observability and MCP tools (Datadog, LangSmith, Corridor) run in the LangGraph server process and never expose their credentials to the sandbox, with an intentionally read-only surface, because the content they return is attacker-influenceable and could carry prompt-injection payloads.

Untrusted external GitHub comment content is wrapped in reserved <dangerous-external-untrusted-users-comment> trust tags, and sanitize_github_comment_body strips those reserved tags from raw comment bodies so external content cannot spoof the trust wrapper.

Dashboard origin enforcement has an explicit local-development fail-open default: require_same_origin does nothing if no DASHBOARD_BASE_URL or DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS origin is configured; otherwise unsafe cookie-authenticated requests need an allowed Origin/Referer, while create_app enables credentialed CORS only for configured origins and rejects a wildcard origin.

Dashboard session cookies are HttpOnly; HTTPS DASHBOARD_API_BASE_URL produces Secure, SameSite=None session cookies for cross-origin dashboard use, while local HTTP uses non-secure SameSite=Lax, and the OAuth state cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, auth-path scoped, and limited to the state TTL.

Focused dashboard tests verify redirect allowlisting and state/PKCE protections, while organization-gate tests cover configured membership decisions, multi-org allowlisting, blank or unset fail-open behavior, and the once-per-process warning.
